angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,628,003 km at 99.01 pc = 0.22 mas. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of the fit's two radii; no interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 10.0997 +/- 0.0293 mas (same row, RUWE 1.23): 99.01 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius: WASP-189 is a rapid rotator. Deline et al. (2022), A&A 659, A74 fit the CHEOPS transits of WASP-189 b with a gravity-darkened oblate star: equatorial radius 2.363 solar radii and a polar radius 2.88% smaller (Table 3), so a polar radius of 2.2949. The record's radius is the volume-equivalent sphere of those two, (2.363^2 x 2.2949)^(1/3) = 2.3401 solar radii at 695700 km per solar radius (https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202142400); the scene draws the flattening, with the equatorial radius on the outline. Mass 2.03 +/- 0.066 solar masses from Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 8000 +/- 80 K from Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis, the spin axis measured against WASP-189 b's orbit, is up.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Lendl et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-189 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass 2.03 and the radius 2.36 solar radii of Lendl et al. 2020, the sphere the limb law was read for, log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.000, rounded to two decimals
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, HD 133112: main object type PM*, High Proper Motion Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-189 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.29 dex, from Lendl et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-189 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 1.31471, from Deline et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...659A..74D/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-189 (pscomppars): age 0.73 Gyr, from Lendl et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-189 (pscomppars): rotation period 1.198 d, from Deline et al. 2022 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022A&A...659A..74D/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-189 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 93.1 km/s, from Lendl et al. 2020 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020A&A...643A..94L/abstract)

shape.qualification: A flattened sphere, the polar radius 2.88% smaller than the equatorial (Deline et al. (2022), A&A 659, A74), colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json) and darkened by latitude from the same fit. No image of the photosphere exists.
